purpose: Returns the stable KVM API version (always 12 since the API stabilized). Firecracker calls this at init and aborts if the value differs — earlier (2.6.20/2.6.21) versions are unsupported.

Probe whether the host KVM supports a given KVM_CAP_*. System-fd form returns the global default; VM-fd form may return a per-VM value (e.g. KVM_CAP_NR_VCPUS). Firecracker probes capabilities at init and refuses to start if a required one is missing.

examples.scenario: Verify userspace memory regions are supported (always true on modern kernels)

purpose: Create a new VM. Returns a VM fd. machine_type identifier is 0 for default; on aarch64 encodes IPA size with KVM_VM_TYPE_ARM_IPA_SIZE().

examples.expected_output: Non-negative fd on success; -EINVAL/-ENOMEM on failure

purpose: Create a vCPU. Returns a vCPU fd. vcpu_id starts at 0 and must be < KVM_CAP_MAX_VCPUS. Firecracker creates one vCPU thread per ID; each thread runs KVM_RUN in a loop.

examples.expected_output: Non-negative fd; -EINVAL on duplicate id, -E2BIG on exceeding limit
examples.scenario: Per-vCPU init in Firecracker's vmm thread

purpose: Returns the size (in bytes) of the kvm_run struct that userspace must mmap on each vCPU fd. Firecracker calls this once and reuses the size for every vCPU.

examples.invocation: size = ioctl(kvm_fd, KVM_GET_VCPU_MMAP_SIZE); mmap(NULL, size, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, vcpu_fd, 0)
examples.scenario: vCPU init — get the kvm_run shared region

purpose: Map a host userspace memory range into the guest physical address space. Slot ID identifies the region; size 0 deletes a slot. Firecracker registers one large region for guest RAM; snapshot restore replays the same regions.

flags.name: slot
flags.doc: Region slot ID. Reuse to overwrite.

flags.name: flags
flags.doc: Bitmask. Set LOG_DIRTY_PAGES for snapshot diffing.

flags.name: memory_size
flags.doc: Size in bytes; 0 to delete the slot.

examples.expected_output: 0 on success; -EINVAL on bad alignment; -EFAULT on bad userspace_addr

purpose: Like KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION but supports guest_memfd-backed regions (KVM_MEM_GUEST_MEMFD flag) for confidential-VM cases. Available when KVM_CAP_USER_MEMORY2 is supported.

flags.name: guest_memfd
flags.doc: Optional guest_memfd file descriptor when KVM_MEM_GUEST_MEMFD is set.

purpose: Atomically copy + clear the dirty-page bitmap for a memory region. Backbone of incremental snapshots — Firecracker calls this per region during a diff snapshot.

flags.name: dirty_bitmap
flags.doc: Userspace buffer; one bit per 4 KiB page.

examples.expected_output: 0 on success; bitmap populated with one bit per page
examples.scenario: Capture pages dirtied since last snapshot

purpose: Clear specific bits of the dirty bitmap without copying. Used with KVM_DIRTY_LOG_MANUAL_PROTECT_ENABLE / KVM_DIRTY_LOG_INITIALLY_SET to decouple read and clear (lets userspace read first, then selectively clear after persisting).

Enter the guest. Returns when the vCPU exits; userspace inspects kvm_run.exit_reason, handles the exit (MMIO/PIO/SHUTDOWN/etc.), and re-enters. The entire CPU-virt fast path. ALL guest execution happens between calls to this ioctl.

examples.expected_output: 0 on normal exit; -EINTR if signal pending; -EFAULT/-ENOMEM on hard error

purpose: Inject a synchronous interrupt vector into the guest. Used when Firecracker has a userspace-emulated PIC (rarely — Firecracker prefers in-kernel irqchip). Asserting an in-kernel-PIC IRQ uses KVM_IRQ_LINE instead.

examples.expected_output: 0 on success; -EEXIST if already pending; -EINVAL on bad vector

purpose: Assert or deassert an in-kernel-irqchip IRQ. Faster than KVM_INTERRUPT because it doesn't context-switch the vCPU. Firecracker uses this for serial-console TX-ready and other userspace-driven IRQs.

Instantiate the in-kernel PIC + IOAPIC + LAPIC (x86) or pre-bind preparation for ARM GIC creation via KVM_CREATE_DEVICE. Must be called BEFORE creating any vCPU. Firecracker always creates the in-kernel irqchip — userspace-irqchip mode is too slow.

examples.expected_output: 0 on success; -EEXIST if already created; -ENOTTY if KVM_CAP_IRQCHIP missing
examples.scenario: Firecracker VM init, before vCPU creation

purpose: Install or replace the GSI routing table — maps GSIs to in-kernel IRQchip pin / MSI / HV SINT. Firecracker programs this so MSIs from VirtIO devices land directly on the right vCPU.

flags.name: entries
flags.doc: Variable-length array; each entry has gsi + type + (irqchip|msi|hv_sint) union.

examples.expected_output: 0 on success; -EINVAL on overlapping GSI; -ENOMEM if too many entries
examples.scenario: Set up MSI routes for VirtIO interrupts

purpose: Inject an MSI directly without going through the routing table. Useful for one-shot interrupts (e.g. VirtIO config-change) that don't have a stable GSI binding.

Bind an eventfd to a GSI. When userspace writes to the eventfd, KVM raises the IRQ on the configured GSI without involving the writing thread further. Backbone of low-latency device-event IRQ delivery.

flags.name: flags
flags.doc: DEASSIGN to remove; RESAMPLE for level-triggered with explicit rearm fd.

flags.name: resamplefd
flags.doc: eventfd that signals when the IRQ has been EOI'd.

examples.scenario: Wire VirtIO ring-event eventfd to its IRQ

purpose: Bind an eventfd to be signaled when the guest writes a specific value (or any value) to a specific MMIO/PIO address. Lets the kernel short-circuit doorbell writes — no exit to userspace, just signal the device thread.

flags.name: datamatch
flags.doc: Required value; if absent, any write triggers.

examples.scenario: Wire VirtIO-MMIO doorbell write (queue notify) to a device-thread wakeup eventfd

purpose: Set the general-purpose register file (RAX..R15, RIP, RFLAGS) for the vCPU. Used at boot to set up the entry point and during snapshot restore.

examples.scenario: Set guest entry point at boot or restore

purpose: Read the GPR register file. Used by snapshots to checkpoint vCPU state and by the GDB debug stub.
Set special registers — segment selectors, control registers (CR0..CR4, CR8), GDTR/IDTR, EFER, APIC base. Used at boot to set up protected/long mode and during snapshot restore.

examples.scenario: Set up long mode at boot

purpose: Read special registers. Pairs with KVM_SET_SREGS for snapshot save.
Bulk-write MSRs. Variable-length kvm_msrs struct: nmsrs followed by entries[]. Returns the count actually written; entries past the failure point are skipped.

examples.expected_output: Number of MSRs successfully written; -EFAULT on bad pointer

purpose: Bulk-read MSRs. Pre-fill entries with the MSR indices to read; KVM populates the .data fields.
Enumerate MSRs the host KVM knows about. Variable-length result. Firecracker uses this to build the snapshot MSR set, intersected with CPU-template-allowed MSRs.

examples.expected_output: Number of MSRs in nmsrs; indices in entries[]

purpose: Define the CPUID leaves the guest sees. Variable-length: nent + entries[] (function/index/flags/eax/ebx/ecx/edx). Firecracker computes this from the chosen CPU template and the host's KVM_GET_SUPPORTED_CPUID intersection.

examples.expected_output: 0 on success; -E2BIG if too many entries
examples.scenario: Apply CPU template at vCPU init

purpose: Enumerate CPUID features KVM knows it can virtualize on this host. Firecracker uses the result as the universe from which CPU templates pick.
Set legacy FPU/SSE state (fxsave-format). Snapshots use this on hosts without XSAVE2 support.
Read legacy FPU/SSE state.
Set extended-state (XSAVE) area. Variable-size — query KVM_CHECK_EXTENSION(KVM_CAP_XSAVE2) for the size on this host. Required for AVX/AVX-512 state.
Read extended-state area. Buffer size from KVM_CAP_XSAVE2 query.
Set the extended control registers (XCR0). Determines which XSAVE features are enabled. Restored as part of snapshot.

examples.expected_output: 0 on success; -EINVAL on bad XCR0 mask

purpose: Read extended control registers.
Restore Local APIC register file (1 KiB). Required for snapshot consistency — preserves pending interrupts and timer state.
Read Local APIC register file.
Set vCPU MP state (RUNNABLE / HALTED / etc.). Snapshot restore uses this so a halted vCPU stays halted on resume.

flags.name: mp_state
flags.doc: Enum: RUNNABLE, UNINITIALIZED, INIT_RECEIVED, HALTED, SIPI_RECEIVED, STOPPED, CHECK_STOP, OPERATING, LOAD.

purpose: Read vCPU MP state.
Restore pending exceptions, interrupts, NMIs, and SMI state. Critical for snapshot consistency — without this, an in-flight exception is lost on resume.
Read pending exception/interrupt/NMI/SMI state.
Set debug registers DR0..DR7. Used by snapshot restore and by the GDB stub for hardware breakpoints.

examples.scenario: Snapshot restore or GDB hw-breakpoint set

purpose: Read debug registers.
Configure guest debug — single-step, software breakpoints, hardware breakpoints. When set, the vCPU returns KVM_EXIT_DEBUG to userspace on debug events. Powers `firecracker --gdb-socket` mode.
Set the guest's TSC frequency. Required for snapshot restore on a host with a different TSC frequency. KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL must be supported.

examples.scenario: Snapshot restore on host with different TSC

purpose: Read the guest's TSC frequency in kHz.

examples.expected_output: Frequency in kHz, or 0 if unset; -ENOTTY if unsupported

purpose: ARM-only. Configure the vCPU's target processor and feature flags before first KVM_RUN. Firecracker calls this for each ARM vCPU during init.
ARM-only. Returns the preferred CPU target for this host (used as input to KVM_ARM_VCPU_INIT).
Create an in-kernel device. On ARM, used for the GIC (KVM_DEV_TYPE_ARM_VGIC_V3) and PMU. Firecracker uses this only on ARM.

flags.name: flags
flags.doc: KVM_CREATE_DEVICE_TEST to probe support without creating.

examples.expected_output: 0 on success; dev.fd usable for KVM_SET_DEVICE_ATTR

purpose: Configure an in-kernel device. ARM GIC distributor base address, redistributor regions, etc., are set this way.

x86 Intel-only. Set the address of a 3-page region used by Intel VT-x for guest-state save (TSS area). Must be set before first KVM_RUN. Firecracker hardcodes this to 0xfffbd000 (matches QEMU convention).
x86 Intel-only. Set the address of a 1-page identity map for guest paging during early boot. Firecracker sets this to 0xfffbc000 (page below TSS area).
Create the in-kernel Programmable Interval Timer (8254). Firecracker uses this for legacy timer interrupts; the alternative (userspace PIT) would generate excessive vCPU exits.
Set the kvmclock value. Used during snapshot restore to maintain monotonic guest time across pause/resume.

examples.scenario: Snapshot restore — adjust guest's view of wall time

purpose: Read the current kvmclock value. Snapshot save records this.
